key_insight: LLM-BlockFE turns long unstructured text into frozen executable feature programs offline, so risk-control models can gain predictive text-derived features without paying LLM latency at inference.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for production systems that need structured, low-latency features from text while keeping deployment cost and real-time reliability compatible with industrial risk-control workflows.
method: Incrementally builds feature programs by appending immutable code blocks guided by an LLM.
Uses downstream model performance to score candidate features during offline search.
Adds block-level rollback and interleaved multi-trajectory search to avoid greedy dead ends and redundant exploration.
evidence_signal: Across two public and two private datasets, the method improved AUC by 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline, and deployed financial applications saw KS gains of 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on offline search and fixed program blocks, it may require careful validation to ensure the learned features remain stable and generalize when text distributions shift.
paper_title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
